decisions.reason: The profile title, summary, and listed denials are supported by the source.
The Harbor Tools role and dates, personal work on Dispatch Loom, training, and handbook are supported. The improvement is correctly described as a team result.

The source says operators preferred a visible warning, not that they used visible warnings. It also asks to distinguish operational use from an externally sold product without explicitly establishing that the tool was not sold externally; the summary and claim present these as settled facts.
The reconciliation-time change, six weekly runs, team attribution, personal contribution, coworkers’ changed habits, and correction of the earlier figure are supported.
The source supports personally training 12 coworkers in two workshops and writing the handbook; it also says exact workshop dates are unavailable.
The source explicitly supports using Python to write the Dispatch Loom parser.
The source explicitly supports writing SQL checks for Dispatch Loom.
The source explicitly supports using PostgreSQL for the production database.
The source explicitly supports using Git for version control and places it in the Collaboration skill category.
The source supports personally training dispatch coworkers and places coworker training in the Collaboration skill category.
The degree, institution, and dates are explicitly stated.
The source supports the certificate and award date, and clarifies that it was a course completion rather than a professional license.
